classification.difficultyReason: Account for a delayed departure and determine when two constant-speed journeys reach the same position.

content.prompt: One car travelling at 80 km/h leaves Melbourne at 8 a.m. It is followed at 10 a.m. by another car travelling on the same road at 110 km/h. At what time will the second car overtake the first?

answer.short:
3:20 p.m.

Equate the distances travelled, allowing for the first car’s two-hour head start.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the number of hours after 10 a.m. At overtaking, both cars have travelled the same distance from Melbourne.
$$\begin{align*}110t&=80(t+2)\\110t&=80t+160\\30t&=160\\t&=\frac{160}{30}\\t&=5\frac{1}{3}\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$
The second car overtakes the first 5 hours 20 minutes after 10 a.m., at **3:20 p.m.**
